headline: New Jersey Permanently Houses Over 2,500 Veterans
meta_description: New Jersey has effectively ended veteran homelessness statewide, permanently housing more than 2,500 veterans since November 2024.
summary_short: New Jersey has effectively ended veteran homelessness statewide, permanently housing more than 2,500 veterans since November 2024 with over $30 million in funding.
body:
New Jersey has effectively ended veteran homelessness statewide, permanently housing more than 2,500 veterans since November 2024.

The achievement represents a significant milestone in the state's efforts to support those who served in the military. More than $30 million in combined state and federal funding made the permanent housing initiative possible, demonstrating a coordinated commitment to addressing homelessness among veterans.

The scale of the accomplishment—housing 2,500 individuals in just a few months—reflects both the urgency of the crisis and the power of sustained, well-resourced intervention. By moving veterans into permanent housing rather than temporary shelters, New Jersey has created stability that allows former service members to rebuild their lives and access additional support services more effectively.
quick_facts: More than 2,500 veterans permanently housed since November 2024
Over $30 million in state and federal funding deployed
New Jersey effectively ended veteran homelessness statewide
